issues.t: Power module (TIPM) failure causes random electrical faults
issues.sym: The horn honks on its own, wipers or washers run by themselves, headlights or dome lights flash, doors lock and unlock, and warning lights fill the dash. Some trucks won't start or stall.
issues.why: The Totally Integrated Power Module (TIPM) under the hood is the fuse and relay box that also has its own computer. On the Nitro its internal circuits and relays fail, sending power to the wrong places or cutting it off.
issues.next: Have a shop scan the body and TIPM codes before replacing parts. Pulling the horn fuse can stop a stuck horn for now. A new or properly remanufactured and programmed TIPM is the usual fix.

issues.t: Engine stalls or shuts off while driving
issues.sym: The engine cuts out at low speed or in traffic, often with dash lights flickering and the A/C or windows acting up at the same moment. Sometimes it restarts right away and sometimes it won't.
issues.why: Most reports trace back to the TIPM power module losing power to the fuel pump or engine computer. Early 2007 trucks also had TIPM software that could stall the engine (covered by a recall).
issues.next: Stalling while driving is dangerous, so get it checked promptly. Ask a dealer to confirm all recalls are done, then have the TIPM and fuel pump relay circuit tested.

issues.t: Transmission shudder, slipping or hard shifts
issues.sym: A shudder or vibration at low to moderate speeds under light throttle, slipping between gears, harsh or delayed shifts, or hesitation pulling away.
issues.why: The torque converter clutch and the transmission's shift programming are the usual causes. Chrysler released computer reflashes for shudder and surge, and some trucks needed a new torque converter.
issues.next: Check the transmission fluid level and condition, then ask a dealer whether software updates are available for your truck. If the shudder stays after an update, have the torque converter inspected.

issues.t: Automatic transmission whine or failure
issues.sym: A whining or howling noise from under the truck, the transmission getting stuck in one gear (limp mode), or no upshifts on the highway.
issues.why: Internal wear in the automatic transmission. Owners report failures from about 50,000 to 95,000 miles, often after earlier shudder or hard-shift complaints.
issues.next: Stop towing or driving hard and get a transmission scan and fluid check. If it is stuck in one gear, a shop needs to check whether it is an electrical fault or internal damage before rebuilding.

issues.t: Rear differential seal leak and bearing failure
issues.sym: Gear oil drips near the rear axle, a whine or growl from the rear that changes with speed, and in bad cases the rear wheels can lock up.
issues.why: The rear axle pinion seal leaks, and if the gear oil runs low the bearings and gears wear and can seize.
issues.next: Check under the rear axle for wet spots and have the gear oil level checked. A leaking seal is a fairly cheap fix; waiting until it howls can mean a full rebuild or a new axle.

issues.t: Dropped valve seat and misfire on the 3.7L V6
issues.sym: A check engine light with a misfire, a ticking or knocking sound, and a sudden loss of power. The engine may run on five cylinders.
issues.why: The 3.7L runs hot, and a pressed-in valve seat can loosen and come out of the cylinder head. That kills compression in one cylinder and can damage the piston.
issues.next: If the check engine light flashes, pull over when it's safe and turn the engine off. A compression test will show whether a valve seat has dropped. Usually the cylinder head must be rebuilt or replaced, and if the piston is damaged the engine may need replacing.

issues.t: Heat shield can rub through the driveshaft (recall)
issues.sym: A scraping or rubbing noise from under the middle of the truck. If the driveshaft breaks there is a loud bang, loss of drive, and the airbags may go off.
issues.why: A heat shield under the truck can sag and rub on the driveshaft, wearing it until it breaks. A broken shaft can hit the floor hard enough to set off the airbags. Recall 13V-121 covers 2007-2008 two-wheel-drive Nitros.
issues.next: Run your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls. The dealer installs a support bracket for free. If you already hear scraping, have the driveshaft inspected.

issues.t: Fuel spits back at the pump or tank cracks near the filler
issues.sym: The pump nozzle keeps clicking off or fuel spills out while filling, sometimes with an EVAP or gas cap warning. Some owners find a crack at the top of the tank near the filler neck.
issues.why: A blocked vent or fault in the tank's evaporative (EVAP) venting stops air from escaping as fuel goes in. In some cases the tank itself was faulty and had to be replaced.
issues.next: Fill slowly in the meantime and don't top off. Have the EVAP vent lines and tank checked; spilled fuel is a fire risk, so don't put it off.

issues.t: Power window regulator breaks or window won't go up
issues.sym: A window drops into the door, goes down but won't come back up, grinds or clicks, or only works from the driver's switch.
issues.why: The window regulator's cable and plastic pulleys break. Less often, the driver's master switch fails.
issues.next: Tape or cover the window if it won't close. A shop will test the switch first, then replace the regulator (often sold with the motor) if the cable has snapped.

issues.t: Heater fan stops working or works only on high
issues.sym: No air from the vents at any setting, or the fan only blows on the highest speed.
issues.why: The blower motor wears out, or the blower resistor or fan switch fails, which leaves only the high-speed circuit working.
issues.next: If it works only on high, the resistor is the likely part. If it never runs, a shop will check power at the blower motor before replacing it.

issues.t: A/C blows warm air
issues.sym: The air conditioning blows warm or only slightly cool air, sometimes after working fine on a cool morning.
issues.why: Refrigerant leaks at lines and O-rings, a failed A/C clutch relay or compressor, or a bad blend door are the reported causes.
issues.next: Have a shop check the refrigerant charge with leak dye before simply refilling it. A relay is a cheap fix; a compressor costs much more.

issues.t: No start from anti-theft key system
issues.sym: The engine won't start or cranks and then dies, and the security light may flash. Remote locking may also stop working.
issues.why: The anti-theft key module (SKREEM/WCM) can lose communication with the key, sometimes after static discharge, so the engine computer blocks starting.
issues.next: Try the spare key. If it still won't start, a dealer or locksmith with a scan tool can check the immobilizer and reprogram or replace the module.

issues.t: Power door locks stop working or cycle on their own
issues.sym: One or more doors won't lock or unlock with the switch or remote, or the locks cycle by themselves.
issues.why: Door lock actuators wear out. Locks that cycle on their own usually point to the TIPM power module.
issues.next: Note which doors are affected. One dead door is usually its actuator; random locking on all doors calls for a TIPM check.

issues.t: Rear brakes and rotors wear out early
issues.sym: Grinding or squealing from the rear, or being told the rear rotors are worn out well before the front brakes.
issues.why: Owners report the rear rotors and pads wearing faster than expected, and sticking calipers causing uneven pad wear.
issues.next: Ask for pad and rotor measurements at each oil change. If one side wears faster, have the calipers and slide pins checked.

issues.t: Steering wheel emblem can come loose in an airbag deployment (recall)
issues.sym: The emblem in the middle of the steering wheel may be loose or missing. There may be no other sign.
issues.why: The emblem or its nuts can come off and fly toward the driver if the airbag deploys. Recall 20V-396 covers 2007-2011 Nitros.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer installs a new driver airbag cover for free.

issues.t: Front head restraint pops forward on its own
issues.sym: A front headrest suddenly snaps forward with a bang while driving or parked and won't go back.
issues.why: The active head restraint is spring-loaded to move forward in a rear crash. A striker pin in the release mechanism can let go without a crash. Chrysler extended the warranty on this part.
issues.next: Don't force it back. Ask a dealer about the active head restraint warranty extension for your VIN.

issues.t: Active head restraints may not deploy in a crash (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning. The front headrests may not move forward in a rear impact.
issues.why: A fault in the active head restraint mechanism could stop it deploying in a rear crash. Recall 13V-282.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The repair is free at a dealer.

issues.t: Steering column rivet may be missing (recall)
issues.sym: No sign while driving. The steering column may not absorb impact correctly in a frontal crash.
issues.why: A rivet in the steering column may be missing or installed wrong on some 2011 trucks. Recall 11V-315.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls; the dealer inspects and repairs it free.

issues.t: ABS hydraulic unit can leak brake fluid (recall)
issues.sym: Brake fluid level drops, the brake pedal feels soft or travels farther, or the brake warning light comes on.
issues.why: A defect in the ABS hydraulic control unit on some 2010 trucks could let brake fluid escape. Recall 10V-315.
issues.next: A soft pedal is a safety issue; don't drive it far. Check your VIN for this recall.

issues.t: Brake booster pushrod clip may come off (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning, but if the clip comes off the brake pedal can suddenly stop working.
issues.why: A retaining clip that connects the brake pedal to the brake booster rod may not have been installed correctly. Recall 10V-009.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls; the dealer inspects and fixes it free.

issues.t: Wipers can stop working (recall)
issues.sym: The windshield wipers quit, often after heavy use of the intermittent (delay) setting.
issues.why: Frequent use of the delay setting could damage the TIPM's wiper control so the wipers stop altogether. Recall 09V-438 added relays and new TIPM software.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall. If the wipers fail, pull over somewhere safe when visibility is poor.

issues.t: ABS software can delay braking (recall)
issues.sym: A short delay before the brakes respond, most likely when coasting uphill.
issues.why: Software in the anti-lock brake module could cause a brief braking delay. Recalls 06V-493 and 07V-434 reprogram the module.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls; the reprogramming is free.

issues.t: Power module software can stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: The engine can stall without warning under certain conditions.
issues.why: Some early 2007 trucks had TIPM software that could shut the engine off. Recall 07V-291 reprograms it.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall. If yours still stalls after the update, have the TIPM tested.

issues.t: Parking brake may not hold on manual-transmission models (recall)
issues.sym: The parking brake feels weak and the truck may creep when parked on a slope.
issues.why: The clutch drum inside the parking brake lever could distort on Nitros with a manual transmission. Recall 08V-525 replaces the lever assembly.
issues.next: Leave it in gear and turn the wheels toward the curb when parking on a hill until the recall is done.
